data.title: Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack
data.description:
Microsoft said it had restored Microsoft 365 services after a global outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other applications for more than 24 hours, reiterating that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.

On Saturday, the company said it had “restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” directing customers to incident MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

On Friday, Microsoft said that the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that emerged after a recent network change. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents,” the company said.

The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and restored services gradually, checking stability before proceeding to the next stage. Microsoft apologized for the disruption and said it would publish a full post-incident report once its review is complete.

The outage began Thursday, disrupting access to Exchange Online mailboxes and features linked to Outlook, Teams and Microsoft Copilot. Government agencies in Japan, Singapore and the United States experienced email problems, while connections between Microsoft 365 and AI assistants were also affected.

OpenAI said the Microsoft 365 connector in ChatGPT was operating normally again, while Anthropic also marked its Microsoft 365 connector and Claude for Outlook incident as resolved.

data.title: AI Agents Process 6.4 Million x402 Payments, but News Is Missing From Top Purchases
data.description:
AI agents made 6.4 million x402 payments on Solana and Base from July 23 to August 26, 2026, but news products were absent from the most-called paid resources. The figures come from BeInCrypto Research’s State of AI Agent Payments 2026 report, according to BeInCrypto. The payments totaled $119,947; 90.8% were below one cent and accounted for 10.7% of the value. Solana recorded 94.5% of transactions in eight days, from August 19 to 26.

The report’s x402 catalogue listed 14,791 paid resources across 1,610 hostnames from August 16 to September 15, 2026. Its most-called resource was a two-cent AI-generated token safety check; web searches, Twitter searches and webpage reads also ranked in the top 10, but no news product did. Yana Prikhodchenko said agents could buy individual articles with stablecoins through x402, without subscriptions. Meanwhile, Google Search referrals to more than 2,500 news sites fell 33% between November 2024 and November 2025. ChatGPT referrals are growing, but Google still sends about 500 times as many readers. Only a fifth of digital leaders surveyed by the Reuters Institute expect AI licensing deals to generate substantial revenue.

data.title: In Jensen Huang's Ouster, Tech Billionaires See a Mistake-and a Lesson — WSJ
data.description:
By Rolfe Winkler

In Jensen Huang, some of America sees a chief executive who was justly tossed from his company for affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and one of his own employees.

Many of his tech-billionaire peers see a brilliant founder who was railroaded.

Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, Travis Kalanick and Joe Gebbia are among the Silicon Valley billionaires who have taken issue with Huang's ouster from the company Thursday.

On X, Musk posted that he would sign a petition reinstating Huang. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao called it a "mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign."

Epic Games founder and Chief Executive Tim Sweeney said Huang's exit at the hands of the board evidenced "serious corporate governance issues" and showed an "Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy."

Underpinning the defense of Nvidia's longtime CEO is the idea that company founders who create billions or trillions of dollars in value and invent useful technologies are uniquely irreplaceable, and ownership structures should insulate them from public or shareholder pressure.

Company boards previously threw out Sam Altman from OpenAI, Travis Kalanick from Uber, and Jobs from Apple — examples all cited by Huang's peers in supporting him.

Jobs ultimately returned to Apple 12 years after he was fired. Altman was back at OpenAI in five days. Kalanick never returned to Uber and on Monday he posted his own 12-step guide to counter boardroom coups.

"Jensen made a rookie mistake. He had a board," wrote Telegram founder Pavel Durov on X. "Founders: Don't have a board."

Huang's stake in Nvidia is estimated to be worth about $140 billion, but it only represents 3.6% ownership of the company, making him vulnerable to shareholder and board sentiment. Nvidia was founded in 1993 and went public in 1999, a year before the dot-com bubble burst.

Beginning with Google's initial public offering in 2004, many founders of the most successful startups have employed dual-class share structures to enable themselves to maintain voting control without owning a majority of company equity. The investors and founders argue that such structures protect against activist investors who might raid a company for its cash.

Partners at venture-capital firms such as Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund have long argued that the best founders are strong personalities pursuing radical, non-consensus ideas and need protection to deliver them.

Marc Andreessen said in 2012 his firm encouraged all of its founders to organize their companies in ways that made it difficult to remove them. "It is unsafe to go public today without a dual-class share structure," he said.

Critics see supervoting shares as a parting gift by venture investors, who often exit after an IPO, demonstrating they are "founder-friendly" so they can win lucrative deals with the next crop of founders.

Huang's value to Nvidia was evident in the sharp decline in its shares after The Wall Street Journal said the board planned to oust him. At their nadir, the company's market capitalization had fallen by more than $500 billion.

Two months ago, Automattic founder Matt Mullenweg was fired by his board following an employee revolt. Mullenweg, whose company contributes to WordPress publishing software, was back in his chair 33 hours and 20 minutes later.

He said boards should not rush to depose a CEO.

"In the fog of war, where there might be incomplete information, it's helpful to give things a few days before drawing final conclusions," he said.

Some Nvidia investors echoed that sentiment, asking the board to reconsider. "We believe it is in the best interest of all stakeholders, and certainly the shareholders of Nvidia, for the board to pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," wrote hedge-fund managers Brad Gerstner of Altimeter and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management.

Write to Rolfe Winkler at Rolfe.Winkler@wsj.com

data.title: Eric Balchunas Calls Nvidia-Driven Market Sell-Off The '280th Nervous Breakdown,' Sees Bitcoin Base In The $60K
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bloomberg's Balchunas said sell-offs like the recent drop in Nvidia were likely "algo-driven."
  • Balchunas said investors in stock exchange-traded funds kept buying through the drop.
  • According to him, Bitcoin was harder to hold through a downturn because it was sentiment-driven.

Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas called the latest market sell-off "the 280th nervous breakdown that the markets have had in the past couple of years," on Friday, while saying Bitcoin (BTC) appeared to have found "a nice base somewhere in the 60s."

Unfazed By NVIDIA Selloff

Speaking with Scott Melker on The Wolf Of All Streets podcast, Balchunas said sell-offs like the recent drop in Nvidia (NVDA) tended to be "algo-driven, headline-driven," and possibly, "short-lived." He said he was "unfazed" and called the hit to the AI trade "more like a speed bump," unless earnings were running into "a real problem over the next couple quarters."

Balchunas said investors in stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) kept buying through the drop. "The Vanguard people, they buy it always," he said. "You cannot shake them." Bitcoin ETFs have not followed the same pattern.

Balchunas estimated year-to-date outflows into the funds at about $1.4 billion. "I mean, it's almost flat. Considering the downturn and the negativity, that's pretty good," he said. "You're treading water in a year."

According to SosoValue data, U.S. Bitcoin ETFs stood at $1.75 billion in net outflows so far this year.

'Elevator Up, Stairs Down'

According to Balchunas, Bitcoin was harder to hold through a downturn because it had no cash flows. However, it was "sentiment-driven," but he added that "with all the bad news thrown at it, it seems to have this nice base somewhere in the 60s."

He described Bitcoin's pattern as the reverse of stocks. "It takes the elevator up and the stairs down," Balchunas said, while stocks take "the stairs up and the elevator down."

Bitcoin’s price was trading at $68,000, down nearly 3% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Pointing to ETFs as a guide, he also explained that the SPDR Gold Shares fund took about eight years to recover from its early peak before more than doubling. "Once the sentiment turns, though, it can go quickly because there's no new supply," Balchunas said.

His comments came as NVDA shares posted their worst week since April last year, falling about 13%, after Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO on Thursday. Balchunas said only "a real problem" with earnings would change his view.

data.title: Tesla Cybercab’s Monthly Subscription Is ‘Too High,’ Elon Musk Admits To MKBHD: ‘Should Match The Cost Of…’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Marques Brownlee highlighted several restrictions on the Cybercab's newly launched order page in a post on X, including its invite-only availability, limited delivery locations and mandatory monthly subscription.
  • Musk responded to the post, saying the vehicle's availability would eventually expand beyond its initial locations.
  • Tesla announced on Friday that select customers are being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use at an estimated purchase price of $29,990.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk has acknowledged that the monthly subscription required to operate the company's Cybercab is currently too expensive, responding to criticism from popular tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee, also known as MKBHD.

Musk suggested that Tesla could bring the fee down significantly, even as the company begins inviting select customers to purchase the fully autonomous vehicle.

Tesla shares declined nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading, while falling another 1% in the afterhours session.

Musk Responds To MKBHD

Brownlee highlighted several restrictions on the Cybercab's newly launched order page in a post on X, including its invite-only availability, limited delivery locations and mandatory monthly subscription.

"Cybercab order page is live. Invite only. Must accept delivery to one of these cities in Texas. Only operates in those existing geofenced areas. Requires a $300 monthly subscription to operate. One vehicle per customer. ‘Estimated delivery’ December," he wrote.

Musk responded to the post, saying the vehicle's availability would eventually expand beyond its initial locations.

"It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval," Musk said.

However, he agreed that the subscription fee needed to come down, acknowledging that the current pricing was too high.

"But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month," Musk added.

The response suggests Tesla could eventually reduce the Cybercab's monthly operating cost from nearly $300 to around $115, although Musk did not provide a timeline for the potential change.

Tesla Cybercab Costs $29,990, But Comes With A Catch

Tesla announced on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990.

The vehicle also requires a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and a mandatory $299 monthly subscription to Tesla's autonomous driving software. The company estimates deliveries will begin in December.

The two-door, two-seater vehicle has no steering wheel or pedals and was previously deployed exclusively in Tesla's Robotaxi fleet.

However, personal ownership comes with geographic restrictions. Tesla's fine print specifies that personally owned Cybercabs will only operate "in supported service areas."

Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, said the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

The initial offering also comes with another limitation, wherein buyers cannot immediately turn their Cybercabs into commercial robotaxis and earn money through Tesla's ride-hailing network.

Tesla's Robotaxi service began operating Model Y SUVs in Austin, Texas, in June 2025 before expanding to other cities in Texas and Florida.

Meanwhile, Musk has previously promised that Tesla owners would eventually be able to add their vehicles to a larger autonomous ride-hailing network.

What Retail Investors Think Of TSLA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Tesla trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

TSLA stock is down 12% year-to-date and 13% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) are up 12% over the past 12 months.

data.title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Groundstop that Upended Flights— WSJ
data.description:
By Alison Sider, Andrew Tangel and Jacob Passy

Federal officials blamed outdated air-traffic control technology for a four-hour groundstop Friday that disrupted thousands of flights around the country.

The drastic step, in response to intermittent air-traffic radio and radar disruptions nationwide, is likely to ripple for days as airlines scramble to reposition aircraft and crews.

Airlines canceled more than 7,500 flights Friday and have already scrubbed 1,800 more on Saturday. Hundreds of flights either turned back or diverted as airports became gridlocked with too many planes on the ground and not enough room to park.

The problem started late Friday afternoon, as the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns. More than 3,500 planes were in the air when the groundstop was issued.

Officials said flights would resume in a slow, controlled manner, with larger passenger planes being prioritized over smaller aircraft. Once the groundstop ended, officials said the FAA was responsible for the turmoil in the nation's airspace it oversees.

"What we have is an incredibly old air-traffic control system," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday in a press conference at the White House, blaming telecom routers that "actually got overloaded with data."

He used the press conference at the White House to plead with Congress to approve funding to make upgrades, which he estimated to cost $50 billion. Without an air-traffic system overhaul, Duffy said outages could happen again — just as there were in the Northeast in September and around Newark Liberty International Airport last year. "You will have more of these," he said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that there was no indication so far the outage resulted from a cyberattack. "There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," he said.

Instead, Mullin attributed the outage to the FAA's "putting patches into the system," and that new equipment and technology was "overwhelming the older system."

Friday was one of the worst days this year for flight cancellations, outranked by a sprawling winter storm in January that resulted in more than 11,600 cancellations in one day, according to aviation-data provider FlightAware.

More than 30% of U.S. departing flights were canceled Friday, according to Cirium, another aviation-data firm.

Even with the departure ban lifted, airlines were preparing for a difficult reset. Some had already scrubbed the vast majority of what they'd planned to fly the remainder of Friday.

With departures halted, airports filled up, leaving little room for more planes to land. The schedule disruptions left planes and crew members out of place for their next flights. That will likely create cascading problems into the weekend.

"It's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened," Duffy said. The secretary encouraged college football teams to contact the FAA to make sure their chartered jets can make their weekend games.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom systems at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online.

The outage appeared to be related to a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to government and industry officials. Some industry officials briefed on the matter said there were timing issues affecting data synchronization throughout the network, which handles crucial radio frequencies and radar feeds air-traffic controllers rely on to talk to pilots and keep aircraft safely separated.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it would work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said: "It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible."

Several airlines issued waivers to allow travelers to rebook flights without penalty. At some airports, including New York's LaGuardia, travelers whose flights were canceled had to wait in long lines to get their checked bags back before they could go home. At Newark airport, security lines were empty as people milled about checking their phones for updates.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he was waiting in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Sara Garven, 66, was traveling with her husband home to Wisconsin from Sarasota, Fla., when the couple were stranded in Baltimore where they had a layover. Overhead announcements were being made roughly every 30 minutes, she said, but the information was no different from what was available online.

"Some are sprinkling the Friday the 13th component, which isn't really helping," she said. "Our main concern is just getting home safely."

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide groundstop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had taken that step in response to the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Write to Alison Sider at alison.sider@wsj.com, Andrew Tangel at andrew.tangel@wsj.com and Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com

data.title: Up 325% in 4 years! Multibagger brewery stock with 1:10 stock split history declares Q2 Results 2026; revenue up 203%
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Multibagger brewery stock Asgard Alcobev shares will be in focus on Monday, November 16, after the brewery company announced a sharp improvement in its September-quarter performance, with revenue more than doubling and net profit rising over 14 times year-on-year.

The stock, which has delivered a multibagger 325% return over four years, also has a 1:10 stock split in its corporate-action history. Its latest results reflect the company's transition towards a brewing-led business following its acquisition of a controlling stake in CMJ Breweries in February 2026.

Asgard Alcobev reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs.48.93 crore in Q2 FY27, up 102.84% from Rs.24.12 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) increased to Rs.2.55 crore from Rs.16.95 lakh, marking growth of 1,402.3%.

EBITDA rose to Rs.7.33 crore from Rs.88.97 lakh a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA increased 42.31%, while its margin expanded to 14.98% from 9.71% in Q1 FY27, an improvement of 527 basis points. PAT grew 50.48% quarter-on-quarter.

Operationally, production increased 18.6% sequentially to 13.82 lakh cases, while dispatches rose 14% to 13.58 lakh cases. Capacity utilisation improved to 78.6% from 63.1%. Can production climbed 67.7% to 4.99 lakh cases, accounting for 36.1% of total production.

For the first half of FY27, revenue stood at Rs.101.96 crore, up 125.17%, while PAT increased 416.08% to Rs.4.24 crore. Gross borrowings declined from Rs.72.54 crore as of March 31, 2026, to Rs.60.84 crore at the end of September.

The company clarified that its line of business changed from February 17, 2026, following its transition to brewing. Consequently, prior-year figures reflect the earlier business, and operating metrics are compared sequentially.

Managing Director Ronak Jain said the quarter's performance reflected improvements in manufacturing operations and profitability following the company's transition to brewing.

"We are encouraged by our strong performance during Q2 FY27, which reflects the progress made in strengthening our manufacturing operations and improving profitability following our transition to the brewing business," Jain said.

The company is targeting EBITDA of approximately Rs.24-28 crore for FY27, supported by higher production volumes, cost efficiencies and operating leverage. It is also working towards increasing annual manufacturing capacity from 8.4 million cases to 10.8 million cases by March 2027, an expansion of approximately 28.6%.

Asgard Alcobev shares ended 1% higher at Rs.35.23 on the BSE on Friday, November 13. The small-cap stock has gained 8% over one month and 17% in three months, but has declined 21% over the past year.

It touched a 52-week high of Rs.63 in December 2025 and a 52-week low of Rs.27.21 in July 2026. The company's four-year return stands at 325%, as highlighted in the stock's multibagger performance.

Asgard Alcobev executed a 1:10 stock split, converting each existing equity share with a face value of Rs.10 into 10 shares with a face value of Rs.1 each.

The company announced the corporate action on October 22, 2024, with January 3, 2025, set as both the ex-split date and record date. Shareholders eligible on the record date received 10 shares for every one share held before the split.

The subdivision adjusted the number of shares and the corresponding market price proportionately, without changing the overall value of an investor's holding solely due to the split.

data.title: Mufin Green Finance gets RBI licence to offer forex, remittance services
data.description:
Mufin Green Finance has received an AD-II licence from RBI, allowing the NBFC to offer forex and remittance services, including medical treatment and education.

The Authorised Dealer Category-II (AD-II) licence allows the company to offer forex conversion, outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) for education, medical treatment, travel and other permissible purposes.

Besides, it can now offer family maintenance remittances, and smaller-ticket trade-related forex services, Mufin Green Finance said in a statement.

The licence opens a new, capital-light business vertical for Mufin Green Finance. Unlike balance-sheet-intensive lending, forex and remittance activities earn fee and commission income, which can scale with limited incremental capital, it said.

Mufin expects this to diversify its revenue streams, reduce its reliance on net interest income, and improve operating leverage and return ratios over time.

"The AD-II licence lets us cater to this growing demand within a regulated framework and extend our ecosystem beyond credit into fee-based services. With this new vertical working alongside our lending business, we see our revenue doubling over the coming year," MD Kapil Garg said.

For the second quarter ended September, 2026, the NBFC's net profit more than doubled to ₹15 crore as against ₹6 crore in the same quarter a year ago.

The total income for Q2 FY27 rose to ₹90 crore from ₹49 crore. Gross NPA improved to 1.77 per cent from 2.37 per cent a year ago, and the capital adequacy ratio stood at 27.73 per cent.

"With this new vertical working alongside our lending business, we see our revenue doubling over the coming year," Mufin added.

data.title: The Chaos and Unexpected Joys of a 19-Hour Global Email Outage — WSJ
data.description:
By Robert McMillan and Angel Au-Yeung

We may live in an age of messaging apps and artificial intelligence, but as about half a billion people discovered this week, good old-fashioned email is pretty important, too.

Starting around 12:30 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, a Microsoft cloud outage knocked the company's email and other services offline. The interruption left swaths of the globe, from healthcare systems to stock exchanges to members of U.K. Parliament, without one of their main tools for communicating. It was the tech world's equivalent of a snow day.

The cause was a server upgrade gone wrong, which then cascaded globally. It was a day reminiscent of the chaos caused in 2024 when the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike crashed 8.5 million Windows systems.

Some users were frustrated. Some simply checked out from work. Others time-traveled back to the telephone era.

Support staff at Envision Technology Advisors, a technical services company, spent yesterday on the phone explaining to customers why their email wasn't working, said Stephen Rose, the company's chief technology officer.

Invision's customers began reaching out early in the day, but with email cut off, they had to turn to the telephone, Rose said. So they called. "Our service desk got totally paralyzed," he said.

Rose's team told callers that Envision wasn't to blame for the outage; Microsoft was. "You hope that it gets out by word of telephone," he said.

Email-deprived entities around the world encouraged customers to reach out via phone, including a water utility in Halifax, Nova Scotia; Detroit's light-rail system; and the East Gippsland region of Australia.

In the U.S., city governments across the country lost email, including Tampa, Fla.; Louisville, Ky.; and the County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner. The House of Representatives was hit too. As was the shipping company Maersk and European exchange operator Euronext. In England, the National Health Service was among several government agencies affected by the outage.

The Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust, a British publicly funded healthcare provider that specializes in mental health services, put out a press release with instructions for patients during the outage. "We would ask that if you need to make a referral today, or you are experiencing a crisis please call our services rather than email at this time," the statement said.

The outage affected a range of Microsoft 365 services, but it centered on Exchange Online and email services, Microsoft said.

Microsoft Teams, a messaging and video chat platform, remained up for many, prompting complaints. "Dear @ Microsoft - you shut down the wrong one. Please turn our email back on and kill Teams. Sincerely, Everyone," wrote Steve Schale, a political strategist based in Florida, on X.

For Jeffrey Michelson, a partner at an accounting firm based in New York City, the outage became a welcome chance to check a few items off his to-do list.

Michelson noticed he wasn't getting any new emails in his inbox in the early afternoon on Thursday. After dropping his daughter off at karate lessons just before sunset, he realized he might not be receiving emails for the rest of the evening.

So he got to work building two bookshelves that his wife had been asking him to complete for a month. "It was kind of nice, I'm not gonna lie," said Michelson. The next day, he woke up in the early morning to 70 unread emails.

Like any snow day, Thursday was fun for some but not so great for people who depended on Microsoft's cloud to get their work done. "Kids love a snow day," Envision's Rose said. "Parents go, 'Oh, my God, I've got these kids inside the house all day.' It's all a matter of perspective."

The outage was more disruptive for some than others. Workhorse Group, an industrial company based in the Detroit area, had to reschedule its third-quarter earnings call to the following week because of the outage.

"Our experience (clearly, like many others) shows how vital it is to have real-time communications, access to documents and the ability to share documents with others," said company spokesman John Williams. He sent his comment via text message.

A Microsoft spokesman said the company wasn't hacked. It was a network upgrade gone wrong, he said. "Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," he said.

The blackout lasted about 19 hours, said Doug Madory, head of internet analysis at the networking company Infoblox.

On X, Microsoft Chief Executive Satya Nadella was silent on the outage. That is not a complete surprise. "I'm an email typist," he told Bloomberg last year.

Write to Robert McMillan at robert.mcmillan@wsj.com and Angel Au-Yeung at angel.au-yeung@wsj.com

data.description:

Care Roofing Inc of Palm Desert Urges Leak Checks Before Winter Rain

14.11.2026 / 10:13 CET/CEST

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

PALM DESERT, CA - November 14, 2026 (NEWMEDIAWIRE) - Care Roofing Inc of Palm Desert, a licensed roofing contractor based at 74710 CA-111 in Palm Desert, is encouraging Coachella Valley homeowners to have their roofs checked before winter storms arrive.

Summer surface temperatures on desert roofs climb well past 150 degrees, and the daily swing into cooler nights keeps roofing materials expanding and contracting for months. Flat and low-slope roofs tend to develop cracked coatings and open seams under that stress. Tile roofs can hide broken or slipped tiles and worn underlayment that only show up as a ceiling stain after a storm. Because heavy rain is infrequent in the valley, many homeowners first learn about a weak spot once water is already inside.

"Our roofs spend all summer taking heat, and then the first real storm of winter shows us every weak spot at once," said Rene Diaz, Owner of Care Roofing Inc of Palm Desert. "A fall inspection lets us find small problems while they are still small and inexpensive to fix."

Care Roofing's roof inspection service checks the roof surface, flashing and penetrations for heat-related wear. When damage turns up, the company's roof leak repair crews trace the water to its source and repair the affected area.

For flat and low-slope roofs, the company applies roof coatings that reseal the surface and reflect sunlight, helping the roof hold up through winter rain and the following summer's heat.

Care Roofing serves Palm Desert, Rancho Mirage, La Quinta, Indian Wells, Palm Springs, Cathedral City, Bermuda Dunes and Thousand Palms. Homeowners can learn more about Rancho Mirage roofing services or call (760) 463-9921 to schedule an inspection.

data.title: Microsoft Service Restored After Widespread Outage, Company Says — WSJ
data.description:
By Joshua Jamerson

Microsoft said it had restored full service to its products as of early Saturday, including processing undelivered emails, bringing to a close a widespread outage that had ricocheted around the world.

The latest

Outage tracker Downdetector showed few reported Microsoft outages as of early Saturday morning. "We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions," Microsoft posted on X.

On its website, the company said all its products were operational, including its Microsoft 365 subscription service for apps such as Teams and Excel that had been widely down. The company also said "the backlog of email messages has been processed."

The context

Downdetector had previously shown hundreds of thousands of users in more than 70 countries reporting problems beginning Thursday and stretching into Friday.

The outages disrupted governments, schools and businesses. Email-deprived entities around the world encouraged customers to reach out via phone, including a water utility in Halifax, Nova Scotia; Detroit's light-rail system; and the East Gippsland region of Australia.

What's next

Insurance payouts to organizations around the world impacted by the outages will likely tally $300 million to $500 million, according to an initial estimate from ratings firm Morningstar DBRS. That is significantly less than the $400 million to $1.5 billion in estimated insured losses from 2024's CrowdStrike outage, Morningstar analysts said.

Some cyber insurance policies cover malicious attacks only, rather than technical issues — the apparent cause of the Microsoft incident. Insurance broker Marsh said the lost profit for which businesses could file a claim would "likely be minimal," as the loss of email services generally has limited financial impact.

Write to Joshua Jamerson at joshua.jamerson@wsj.com

data.title: Microsoft services fully restored after outage
data.description:
Microsoft said Saturday that services are now restored following the major outage that began on Thursday.

“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hourslong episode had impacted some of their operations.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.

The Redmond, Washington-based company apologized on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.

It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

The disruptions offer the latest example of the cascading problems that can erupt when so many communications and technology platforms depend on the same provider. Some lawmakers outside the U.S. have also argued that the outage shows the consequences of overreliance on American tech.

“With no emails coming or going, many office workers feel like they are having a virtual snow day,” said Jeremy Singer, a professor at the University of Glasgow’s School of Computing Science.

Still, he added, “this problem serves to emphasize the dependence we have built on one company’s digital infrastructure, and may lead us to question whether we need more resilience in our IT ecosystem.”

The global reach of the outage was swift. After problems first emerged midday Thursday in the U.S., online tracker Downdetector said it received outage reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour.

The total number of people affected was not clear, but Microsoft said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services.

Microsoft scrambled to recover services

A series of posts by Microsoft 365 on X suggested its engineers struggled to get the problem under control for some time, drawing teasing from other companies and users alike. But the tech giant has said there is “no indication” that the disruptions were caused by malicious activity, specifically noting Friday that the outage was not related to a cyberattack or artificial intelligence agents.

Microsoft said a technical issue arose during an upgrade that followed “a recent network change.” The company added that it restored services gradually, which took longer.

As Microsoft addressed issues affecting its Exchange Online mailboxes, it earlier cited a failure that it said caused a number of its servers to be “unexpectedly unavailable” during automated checks.

For Outlook, many users said they couldn’t send or receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether. Those problems piled up across much of the world into Friday.

Disruptions piled up from the courtroom to the pharmacy

In Britain, the outage brought a halt to a trial in Manchester. Judge Maurice Greene sent jurors home because of delays that he said illustrated the danger of the court’s reliance on technology.

The British government said it was “working closely” with Microsoft to assess any impact on public services but that “robust contingency plans” were in place to minimize disruption.

British police said they were unable to receive crime reports online and urged people to phone in urgent requests. The outage also affected some law enforcement in the U.S. The sheriff’s office in Colorado’s Arapahoe County, for example, noted that online bond payments were affected.

Also in Britain, the National Pharmacy Association warned customers of delays in getting medication. The outage affected the National Health Service and threatened to prevent doctors from emailing prescriptions to pharmacies.

“Please bear with your pharmacy teams today, where waits may be longer than normal and there may be delays to some prescriptions,” a spokesperson said.

Governments in Singapore, Japan, Greece and Norway said the outage affected some of their operations, including email communications for certain ministries or agencies.

And of course, businesses were wracked with disruptions. Hong Kong businessperson Danny Lau, who runs an aluminum company, said his business couldn’t receive updates from its U.S. customers through Outlook.

Some banks in Hong Kong, an Asian financial hub, also saw disruptions.

-- The AP contributed to this report.

data.title: Planning to buy a new Maruti Suzuki car? Here's a list of top five highest-selling cars in October | Details
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Are you planning to buy a new car and considering a Maruti Suzuki model? If so, you may want to take a look at which cars are the top-selling models in the market. From hatchbacks and sedans to SUVs, several Maruti Suzuki models continue to witness strong demand, with at least six models recording sales of over 20,000 units in a single month.

According to a statement from the company, Maruti Suzuki sold a total of 2,76,120 units in October 2026, marking its highest-ever monthly sales volume. Domestic sales also reached an all-time high of 2,16,789 units. Sales to other OEMs stood at 9,459 units, while exports were at 49,872 units. Of the 2,76,120 units, total domestic passenger vehicle (PV) sales stood at 2,12,384. This included passenger cars, utility vehicles and vans.

The Mini, Compact and Mid-Size passenger car segment, comprising Alto, Baleno, Celerio, Ciaz, Dzire, Ignis, S-Presso, Swift and WagonR, recorded sales of 1,00,877 units.

The utility vehicle segment, which includes Brezza, Ertiga, Vitara, Fronx, Grand Vitara, Invicto, Jimny, Victoris and XL6, registered sales of 97,787 units.

Meanwhile, Maruti Suzuki's van segment, comprising the Eeco, recorded sales of 13,720 units.

The latest sales performance also points to sustained interest in its passenger vehicle range. Maruti Suzuki registered a 20.46% year-on-year increase in October 2026. In October 2025, the company recorded sales of 1,76,318 units.

Here's a look at the top five Maruti Suzuki models in terms of sales, which you can consider before deciding which one to buy:

1. WagonR: Taking the top spot on the chart is the WagonR. The company sold 23,747 units of the car in October 2026, compared with 18,970 in the same month last year, registering a 25.18% growth. It also logged a 26.08% jump from the 18,835 units sold in September. According to a RushLane report, WagonR sales accounted for 11.8% of the company's October sales and finished 1,311 units ahead of the Brezza.

2. Brezza: The SUV took second place and sold 22,436 units, marking a jump of 85.85% year-on-year and 43.04% month-on-month. In October last year, the company sold only 12,072 units of the SUV.

3. Baleno: Baleno ranked third, with 20,919 units sold in October, compared with 16,873 units in the same month last year. Although sales increased 23.98% compared with the same month last year, they declined 17.62% from September's 25,392 units. It was the only Maruti Suzuki model to register a month-on-month drop in sales.

4. Dzire: Dzire finished fourth and sold 20,649 units, marking a 0.68% decline year-on-year. However, car sales were up 16.31% compared with September 2026.

5. Ertiga: Ertiga, a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), finished fifth on the list and sold eight units fewer than Dzire in October. It sold 20,641 units, registering marginal growth of 2.76% year-on-year. In October 2025, a total of 20,087 units were sold. However, its month-on-month growth from September was 22.06%.

Maruti Suzuki's October sales figures highlight the continued demand for its hatchbacks, SUVs and MPVs. While WagonR led the list, Brezza recorded the highest year-on-year growth among the top five models. Buyers, however, should also compare factors such as pricing, features, mileage, and their individual requirements before making a purchase.

data.title: Rekha Jhunjhunwala stock VA Tech Wabag: Rs.2,400 cr Saudi project cancelled - Should you buy after 18% rise in 6 months?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Rekha Jhunjhunwala portfolio stock VA Tech Wabag shares are likely to remain in focus on Monday, November 16, after the company disclosed that a major desalination project in Saudi Arabia, valued at approximately Rs.2,400 crore, had been cancelled by the customer, Saudi Water Authority, citing internal reasons.

Rekha Jhunjhunwala holds an 8.0% stake in VA Tech Wabag Ltd as of September 2026.

The shares ended 2% lower at Rs.2,040.10 apiece on the BSE on Friday. The stock had touched a 52-week high of Rs.2,320 in September 2026 and a 52-week low of Rs.1,033.95 in January 2026. Despite the recent decline, it has gained 3.5% in one month, 8% in three months, 48% in six months, 45% in one year and 506% over five years.

In an exchange filing on Saturday, November 14, VA Tech Wabag said it had received the award in July 2025 to execute a 300 million litres per day (MLD) mega seawater desalination plant at Yanbu, Saudi Arabia. Following the award, the company completed the required formalities and executed the contract, which was submitted to the customer for counter-signature and formal commencement of the project.

However, Saudi Water Authority subsequently notified all tender participants through the Kingdom's Etimad electronic government procurement and tendering platform that the tender had been cancelled due to internal reasons attributable to the customer.

Wabag said it was approaching the authority to obtain further clarity on the reasons for the cancellation and determine the next course of action.

The project covered the design, engineering, supply, construction and commissioning of a 300 MLD desalination facility at Yanbu on Saudi Arabia's west coast. Its contract value was approximately $272 million, equivalent to 1.019 billion Saudi riyals or around Rs.2,400 crore.

The development follows a similar setback in December 2024, when the Saudi Water Authority cancelled another 300 MLD desalination project in the country. At the time, the authority had informed tender participants that the cancellation was due to internal administrative procedures.

VA Tech Wabag reported revenue of around Rs.1,000 crore and profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.104 crore in Q2 FY27, with margins at 14.4%.

CFO Skandaprasad Seetharaman expects revenue growth in FY27 to be at the higher end of the company's guidance range of 15-20%. Growth could exceed this range if anticipated orders materialise. The company's order book has crossed Rs.20,000 crore, compared with Rs.7,000-10,000 crore earlier.

"We are very confident with the order book as well as the bid pipeline; the year should also be strong," Seetharaman said.

The company expects to sustain margins in the 13-15% range, while continuing to focus on profitable growth and cash generation.

Motilal Oswal has reiterated its 'Buy' recommendation on VA Tech Wabag, with a target price of Rs.2,529 per share. The brokerage said the company remained well-positioned for sustained growth, supported by regular order inflows and normal project execution, including in the war-affected West Asia region.

The brokerage noted that Wabag's current order book of around Rs.20,000 crore was equivalent to five times its FY26 revenue. Along with a strong bid pipeline, this provides visibility for revenue growth of 20% over the next three to four years, it said.

After delivering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7% in revenue, 17% in EBITDA and 28% in adjusted profit after tax (APAT) over FY21-26, Motilal Oswal expects the respective metrics to grow at CAGRs of 19%, 26% and 23% over FY26-28.

The brokerage also highlighted the company's strong free cash flow generation, net cash position of Rs.1,000 crore and improving return ratios. At 21 times its estimated FY28 price-to-earnings ratio, Motilal Oswal considers the stock attractive.

data.title: Deepak Fertilisers gets relief in ₹215 crore tax case; ITAT dismisses department's appeals
data.description:
Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation (DFPCL) has received relief from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, which dismissed appeals filed by the Income Tax Department for six assessment years from 2013-14 to 2018-19.

The appeals concerned disputed taxable income of ₹215 crore. The tribunal's decision upholds the relief granted to the company by the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), Mumbai, through an order dated January 8, 2026.

The company disclosed the development in a regulatory filing on Saturday, November 14, stating that it received an email from the authority at 1:10 pm on November 13.

Six-year tax dispute ends with department's appeals dismissed

The matter relates to an earlier order covering assessment years 2013-14 to 2018-19, against which the Income Tax Department had approached the ITAT after the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) ruled in favour of DFPCL.

The department's appeals have now been dismissed, confirming the relief granted to the company under the January 8 order.

DFPCL's appeals partly allowed

Separately, the ITAT allowed appeals filed by DFPCL for assessment years 2015-16 and 2016-17 on certain issues. However, these appeals were allowed for statistical purposes, according to the company's filing.

The tribunal's order comes a day after DFPCL reported an 84.7% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹393.8 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹213.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue rose 10.9% to ₹3,334 crore from ₹3,006 crore in Q2 FY26. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 61.4% to ₹749 crore, compared with ₹464 crore in the year-ago quarter.

EBITDA margin expanded to 22.5% from 15.4% in the corresponding quarter last year.

Chairman and Managing Director S.C. Mehta said the company had delivered its best-ever first-half performance despite volatility and supply-chain disruptions arising from the US-Iran conflict.

Mehta attributed the performance to the company's integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG)-to-ammonia-to-downstream value chain, which he said helps mitigate supply and cost volatility and supports profitability across market cycles.

He also pointed to demand from India's mining, crop nutrition and industrial chemicals sectors as key support for the business.

Shares of Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation ended almost flat at ₹1,260 on Friday, ahead of the announcement. The stock has declined about 11% over the trailing 12-month period.

data.title: FTC Sues To Block Covetrus' $3.5 Bln Acquisition Of MWI Veterinary Supply
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Federal Trade Commission or FTC announced that it has filed a lawsuit to block Covetrus Inc. and its owners, Clayton, Dubilier & Rice LLC and TPG Inc., from acquiring MWI Veterinary Supply Inc. from Cencora Inc. (COR) in a deal valued at $3.5 billion.

According to the FTC, the proposed transaction would combine the two largest distributors serving veterinary clinics and large corporate veterinary accounts in the United States. The agency argues that the merger would reduce competition, allowing the combined company to increase costs for veterinary clinics, lower service quality, and ultimately raise prices for pet owners.

The FTC's complaint alleged that Covetrus and MWI are each other's closest competitors in key veterinary distribution markets, making the acquisition potentially harmful to customers that rely on their products and services.

The Commission voted 2-0 to authorize staff to seek a permanent injunction blocking the transaction. The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The FTC's action is backed by the attorneys general of Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, and Texas, who joined the complaint in an effort to stop the deal from proceeding.

data.title: GEMI Stock Extends Losing Streak To Eighth Straight Week, Hits Record Low Despite Drop In Quarterly Loss
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gemini Space Station ended Friday's trading session at $2.3, reaching its record low. 
  • Total revenue fell 19% from a year earlier, while transaction revenue dropped 40%.
  • The revenue came more from its services segment, which includes its credit card business.

Gemini Space Station (GEMI) shares fell for the eighth straight week on Friday, reaching its record low despite the crypto exchange trimming its third-quarter loss and costs for a third consecutive quarter.

GEMI has fallen for eight straight weeks and is down roughly 59% from its late-September high. The biggest weekly drops were seen in mid-to-late October, of around 18% and 15%, followed by around 14% in the week of Nov. 2.

Shares fell more than 3% this week, reaching $2.375, the stock’s lowest close on record. On Friday’s trading session, GEMI stock was down over 9%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GEMI dropped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ zone over the past day, while chatter stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Losses Narrow, Costs Drop

Gemini said total revenue was down 19% from a year ago to $40.9 million and down 10% from the second quarter. The revenue missed the analyst estimate of $43.05 million, according to Koyfin. Gemini reported a loss of $0.46 per share, while Wall Street expected a loss of $0.59 per share, according to Koyfin.

The company said the volume of trades on its platforms fell to $4.5 billion from $16.4 billion a year ago, largely reflecting weaker crypto trading. Gemini said about 26% of the volume came from trades between external customers and its affiliated market maker.

Gemini said exchange revenue fell 47% from a year earlier to $13.4 million, largely due to lower retail activity with transaction revenue declining 40% to $15.9 million. Gemini's prediction markets generated about $0.8 million net of incentives, the company said, up 52% from the second quarter.

Credit Cards Carry More Weight

The move away from trading has made Gemini more dependent on its services segment. The company said services revenue and interest income was $23.3 million, or 59% of net revenue, up from 47% a year earlier.

Credit card revenue was $15.5 million, up 82% year over year. Gemini said the card business still lost money after provisions for bad loans, but the loss shrank to $3.4 million from $10.6 million in the second quarter.

Card charge-offs, or balances written off as uncollectible, rose to $11.5 million from $3.4 million a quarter earlier. Total delinquencies 30 days or more over the same period fell to 6% from 9.4%. Gemini said delinquency was broadly stable at 3.4%, excluding accounts it identified as fraud.

Cameron Winklevoss Doubles Down On Gemini 2.0

The company said staking revenue was down 29% to $4.2 million from a year ago due to lower staked balances and yields.

Gemini ended the quarter with $194.1 million of cash and cash equivalents, up from $188.6 million at the end of June. The company said it increased its credit facility with Galaxy by $35 million after the quarter ended.

President Cameron Winklevoss framed the company's strategy around owning regulated infrastructure. "Gemini 2.0 is our bet that the platforms that last will be the ones that own the regulated infrastructure underneath," he said.

  • Huang also discussed taking legal action against The New York Times after the publication ran an article in October 2025 drawing attention to his public meetings with Alice Huang.
  • The former Nvidia CEO has received support from Elon Musk, Fundstrat’s Tom Lee, Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke, and others, who signed a petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company’s chief.

Former Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang allegedly misled senior company executives about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who was under U.S. investigation for potentially spying for China.

According to a Reuters report citing people familiar with the matter, Huang repeatedly characterized his interactions with Alice Huang as routine business dealings.

Nvidia shares fell more than 2% in Friday’s regular trading, declining over 1% more during the afterhours session.

Huang Described Interactions As Standard Dealings, Says Report

In October, Huang sent two separate messages to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter and Chief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld, describing the interactions as standard dealings with customers.

The report also said Huang had discussed taking legal action against The New York Times after the publication ran an article in October 2025 drawing attention to his public meetings with Alice Huang.

The former Nvidia CEO has received support from Tesla Inc. (TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk, Fundstrat’s Tom Lee, Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke, and others, who signed a petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company’s chief.

Nvidia Board Launches Independent Investigation

The revelations come amid growing scrutiny of Huang's personal relationships and their potential implications for Nvidia.

Huang announced his decision to step down as Nvidia CEO, President, and a member of the board effective immediately on Thursday. He apologized in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and disappointing the company, although he did not specifically name Alice Huang.

CFO Colette Kress has been appointed as the interim CEO while the company continues to search for a successor to Huang.

Apart from Alice Huang, Jensen Huang reportedly had extramarital relationships with two Nvidia employees.

On Nov. 10, Nvidia's independent board members hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation following reports about Huang's relationships with Alice Huang and U.S. authorities' suspicions about her alleged links to China.

Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, has been investigated by U.S. authorities for potentially spying for Beijing, allegations that China has denied.

What Retail Investors Think Of NVDA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Nvidia trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

NVDA stock is down 13% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) are up 12% over the past 12 months.

data.title: Binance targets full reopening of withdrawals by next week
data.description:
Binance said on Saturday that it aims to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week, as operations normalise for the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion stolen from the platform last month.

"This week, we reopened withdrawals for 87 networks. We will aim to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week," the company said in an X post.

Binance resumed withdrawals in phases earlier this month, after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in what experts describe as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever.

The FBI and Binance have said North Korea was responsible for the Binance hack, but Pyongyang has denied that. Blockchain investigation firms have attributed it to a North Korean group known as "TraderTraitor".

In its initial report on how hackers pulled off the heist, Binance detailed a multi-stage hacking endeavour that began in June and set off a series of security breaches culminating in the theft on October 29.

The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact of the hack on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full.

The company's finance chief Kaiser Ng left the company just over a week after the heist, to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance. He was replaced by longtime finance executive Justin Yek, who was most recently vice-president of finance at Airwallex.

data.title: Modi's office summons telecom secretary over use of fake court orders, officials say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Government probes intensifying on why fake court orders led to takedowns
  • Telecom secretary to cut short trip to appear in person at Modi's office
  • Telecoms ministry has begun internal inquiry, police seek records
  • Fake orders removed from government website on Saturday

By Aftab Ahmed, Munsif Vengattil and Aditya Kalra

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office summoned the telecommunications secretary on Saturday to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites based on fake court orders, two government officials said.

The intervention from Modi's office signals intensifying scrutiny after Reuters reported on Wednesday that telecom officials directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites based on fake High Court orders which were emailed to officials by people posing as lawyers.

While online betting is illegal in India, the case has raised concerns that a lack of safeguards in India's content-takedown system could allow falsified court documents to be used to block legitimate websites.

The findings have triggered a criminal investigation by state police into potential forgery and cheating by unidentified people.

Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal to appear and explain the lapse, cutting short Agrawal's trip to another state, said the two government officials with knowledge of the matter.

Agrawal is the most senior bureaucrat in the telecommunications ministry, which oversees everyone from big telecom operators to internet providers.

"The action taken by the Department of Telecommunications against betting accounts was carried out through the relevant field officers," one of the officials said.

Agrawal, his ministry and Modi's office did not respond to requests for comment.

Court precedents generated using AI have caused concerns among judges the world over. India's Supreme Court in July set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments, and a US judge recently disqualified lawyers over use of fabricated legal citations.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the telecoms ministry had initiated an internal investigation into the alleged fraud, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation.

The two state court orders flagged as fake by Reuters, based on comments from police and the court registry, contained fabricated court logos and seals, ​as well as a fake QR code.

They were available publicly on the Department of Telecommunications' website for months, along with correspondence that showed government officials ordering internet providers to remove the websites.

On Saturday, one of the fake court orders was still accessible on the government's website, while one had been removed.

Amid growing concerns over ​fake orders, India's Supreme Court justices last year said such fabrication "bearing forged signatures of Judges strikes at the very foundation of public trust" and "such grave criminal acts cannot be treated as ordinary or routine offences".

data.title: U.S. Wholesale Inflation Hits 6.5%—What It Means for Bitcoin’s Next Move
data.description:
Bitcoin’s inflation problem has a fresh complication. U.S. wholesale prices rose 6.5% over the year to October, their fastest annual increase since November 2022, even as the monthly pace cooled sharply.

The November 13 Producer Price Index release offers ammunition for two competing readings: the latest month was less severe, but the accumulated inflation problem remains substantial. For cryptocurrency investors, the key question is which message carries more weight with the Federal Reserve.

Bitcoin inflation outlook: a slower month, a hotter year

Final-demand producer prices increased 0.3% in October, compared with a revised 1.4% in September. The annual rate nevertheless climbed from 6.3% to 6.5%. These measures answer different questions: the first tracks one month, while the second compares prices with a year earlier.

The measure excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for the month and 4.9% annually. That detail complicates any argument that a softer headline monthly figure settles the inflation debate.

Energy prices at the final-demand level edged lower, while goods and services prices increased. The release therefore does not present a simple picture of falling energy costs eliminating pressure throughout the economy.

The BLS defines PPI as a measure of selling prices received by domestic producers. It is distinct from the prices households pay and from the personal consumption expenditures measure targeted by the Fed. Comparing its 6.5% reading directly with the Fed’s 2% goal would mix different indexes.

The Fed had already warned that a pause was not a pivot

At its October 28 meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate at 3.75%–4%. Two members, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, preferred a quarter-point increase. The committee’s statement said: “Inflation remains elevated.”

That split matters. Holding rates steady can provide time to assess incoming information without signalling that the next move will be a cut. Investors who treat every pause as easing risk misreading the decision.

Governor Christopher Waller made the distinction explicit in his November 10 speech, saying “further tightening of monetary policy will be needed, sooner rather than later.” He supported at least a quarter-point December increase under his expected outlook and said a stronger move might be warranted if inflation proved worse.

Waller spoke before that day’s consumer inflation release and before Friday’s PPI figures. His remarks establish the concerns policymakers brought into this week; they are not a reaction to the new wholesale-price report or a commitment by the full committee.

He also singled out the AI infrastructure buildout as a potential source of price pressure, alongside energy costs. That connects two markets often treated as separate stories: enthusiasm for more computing capacity can support investment while raising concerns about the cost of equipment and power.

For crypto readers, the implication is a feedback loop to watch, rather than a demonstrated cause of Bitcoin’s decline. Strong technology investment is not automatically a signal that financing conditions will become easier for every risky asset.

Why Bitcoin can struggle when inflation rises

Bitcoin’s fixed supply underpins its long-term scarcity argument. Its market price, however, is set by buyers and sellers facing changing financing costs and competing investment choices. Those are separate mechanisms.

If persistent inflation keeps interest rates higher, cash and interest-bearing assets can become more competitive, while borrowing to take market exposure becomes more expensive. That can work against speculative demand even when the underlying inflation story sounds favourable to scarce assets.

It does not follow that every inflation release must push Bitcoin lower. Expectations matter: a troubling number can be less troubling than investors had anticipated. Positioning, liquidity and subsequent policy commentary can also change the response.

That is why this report should not be assigned sole responsibility for a move already under way. BNC’s latest Bitcoin market analysis describes November 13 trading around $68,600–$69,200 alongside negative funding on several exchanges. Those observations document a weak market; they do not isolate the effect of PPI.

Three signals that would clarify the next move

First, watch whether subsequent Fed communication treats the slower monthly increase as progress or focuses on persistent underlying pressure. The next scheduled policy meeting is December 8–9, leaving room for more data and debate.

Second, distinguish price stabilisation from renewed buying. A market can stop falling because leveraged positions have been closed, without attracting enough fresh demand to sustain an advance. ETF flows and spot-market activity would help test that distinction, using figures dated to the same trading session.

Third, assess funding rates alongside price. Negative funding indicates demand for short exposure relative to long exposure in perpetual futures. It can accompany weakness, but it can also leave a market vulnerable to a squeeze if prices recover. It is context, not a forecast.

The strongest reading of Friday’s release is therefore conditional. A slower monthly pace offers evidence that the pressure can ease; the annual rate and underlying measure show why policymakers may remain unconvinced. Bitcoin’s next durable move needs more than a comforting interpretation of one headline.
